analysis.title: Regional Wrap - 6 Nov 2026
key_insights: Asia equities closed sharply lower on 6 Nov as the global AI and tech selloff drove broad de-risking across the region. North Asia was hit hardest, with Korea and Taiwan leading losses on heavy foreign selling in semiconductors.

Japan's Nikkei fell 5.96% to 57,434.77, the deepest one-day drop since April 2025. 222 of 225 components and all 33 Topix sectors declined. For the week the Nikkei fell 9.3%, its worst weekly decline since March 2020.

Taiwan's TAIEX fell 4.51% after futures and TSMC touched limit down. The index is down 20% from its 10/6 high, a technical correction, and is hovering around the 200-day moving average. The OTC index has erased its YTD gain.

Taiwan desk commentary: discussion centered on retail capitulation and a potential short-selling ban. Desk activity was probably the highest in three months, mostly selling and shorting, with buying limited to short covering. Turnover exceeded NT$1tn, up 28% DoD.

KOSPI fell 6.51% and broke below the 5,100 level for the first time since 31 March 2026. Foreigners net sold for a sixth straight session (-$2.0bn today vs -$2.5bn yesterday), concentrated in Tech (-$1.4bn). Local institutions and retail bought the dip.

Korean semis fell 8.4%, and former 'blue sweep' beneficiary sectors also fell (Autos -3.3%, Healthcare -2.8%). Only Telcos and selected Cloud names held up. The desk called it broad de-grossing. There was selective dip-buying in memory names including Hynix, which did not offset outflows. KOSPI turnover was +42.8% vs the 20-day average.

China was more contained. Star 50 and the AI Index fell as much as 5% intraday, but bargain hunting and Beijing's market-support measures pulled the Shanghai Composite to 3,649.18 and the CSI 300 (-1.44%) to 4,054.28. AI hardware names with US exposure led losses (Zhongji -8% to a one-year low, Eoptolink -7%, Zhipu as much as -15.4%).

Hong Kong's HSI fell 1.27%, but the Hang Seng AI Index fell 4%. SJM Holdings fell 11.1% to a record low after a Q3 loss of HK$397m, pulling Macau gaming names down 1-6.5%. HKEX fell 3.1% after Q3 profit of HK$4.86bn missed consensus of HK$4.92bn.

India was the regional outlier. Nifty rose 1.08% and is on course for its best week in about six years (~7% weekly gain). Foreigners bought USD 1.6bn on Thursday, the largest single-day net buy in nearly six years, as funds rotated out of AI-linked positions into financials and domestic exposures. The rupee hit a six-month high of 94.10 per dollar.

Australia was the most resilient developed market (ASX200 -0.49%). Nine Entertainment rose 10.8% on FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth guidance. Macquarie fell after mixed first-half results and an APRA review of its non-bank required capital. Goodman Group fell about 4% on options activity at 3.5x its 20-day average.

ASEAN was mixed. Indonesia's JCI rose 0.07% as policy concerns eased over the commodity export framework, which will monitor rather than centralise exports. Focus is on MSCI's upcoming index review. Thailand's SET fell 2.07% with the regional risk-off tone.

market_movers.rationale: Nine Entertainment (ASX: NEC) rose 10.8% after guiding FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth versus FY26.
Macquarie Group (ASX: MQG) traded lower after mixed first-half results and an APRA review of its non-bank required capital following a Non-Operating Holding Company authority breach.
SoftBank Group fell 10.8% and Advantest fell 5% as AI-linked names led the Japan rout.
SJM Holdings fell 11.1% to a record low of HK$1.085 after a Q3 loss of HK$397m vs a HK$9m profit a year ago.
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing fell 3.1% after Q3 profit fell 1% y/y to HK$4.86bn, slightly below consensus of HK$4.92bn.
Bajaj Finance rose 12.6% for the week after a broker flagged strong topline growth.

sector_views.rationale: Semis fell 8.4% and led the KOSPI lower amid heavy foreign selling, with Tech seeing -$1.4bn of foreign outflow.
Nifty Financials rose 8.7% on the week as foreign flows rotated out of AI-linked positions into financials and domestic exposures.

earnings_insights: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing reported Q3 profit of HK$4.86bn, down 1% y/y, slightly below consensus of HK$4.92bn (reported 6 Nov).
SJM Holdings reported a Q3 loss of HK$397m vs a HK$9m profit a year earlier (reported).
Nine Entertainment guided FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth versus FY26.
Macquarie Group reported mixed first-half results.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The rupee rallied to a six-month high as foreign inflows into Indian equities accelerated.

risk_factors: The global AI and tech selloff continues to spread across Asia equities.
Continued foreign selling in Korea and Taiwan semiconductors.
MSCI's upcoming index review for Indonesia.
APRA review of Macquarie's non-bank required capital.
vol_and_positioning: The Nikkei volatility gauge rose to its highest since 31 March.
Korea: foreigners net sold for 6 consecutive sessions. The desk described broad de-grossing, with front-loaded selling in the morning, much of it from sticky money supplies.
Taiwan: desk described retail capitulation and heavy intraday selling and shorting, with buying mostly short covering.
Goodman Group options activity was 3.5x its 20-day average.
India: foreigners bought USD 1.6bn on Thursday, the largest single-day net buy in nearly six years, as funds rotated out of AI-linked positions.
geopolitical: Beijing's ongoing market-support measures helped mainland indices recover from steeper intraday losses.
Taiwan is discussing a potential short-selling ban.
Indonesia clarified that its planned commodity export framework would focus on monitoring rather than centralising exports through a state entity.
